newsitem.title: USA: Killer executed in Maryland for 1985 murder.
newsitem.headline: Killer executed in Maryland for 1985 murder.

text.p: Flint Gregory Hunt was executed by lethal injection in the Maryland Penitentiary early on Wednesday for killing a Baltimore police officer in 1985.
Hunt, 38, shot and killed Vincent Adolfo, 25, who was chasing him in connection with a stolen car.
"The event today was not about vengeance, it was about justice -- justice that took 11 and one-half years, said Gary McLhinney, president of Baltimore's Fraternal Order of Police.
Hunt was pronounced dead at 12:27 a.m. EDT (0427 GMT).
His last meal consisted of vegetarian hot dogs, soup, a salad and four slices of bread, prison officials said.
Hunt's attorneys complained that he was unconscious when the curtains to the death chamber were opened for witnesses.
Two weeks ago, Hunt married an Annapolis woman with whom he had been corresponding for a year. It was not known whether she was at the prison.
The last execution in Maryland was in 1994. The last execution before that occurred in 1961 in the state's gas chamber.

Civil rights advocates petitioned the courts to stop the execution, saying Maryland's death row was disproportionately filled with blacks who killed whites. Of the 17 people on death row, 14 are black.

Hunt was the last Maryland death row prisoner who had the option to choose between the gas chamber and lethal injection. He earlier opted for the gas chamber to show the brutality of execution; he changed his mind last week.
Maryland Gov. Parris N. Glendening refused to grant a stay of execution and a Baltimore Circuit judge had refused to allow Hunt to change his choice of the method of execution.
Last Friday, the Maryland Court of Appeals overruled the lower court and opproved Hunt's choice of lethal injection.
